subject: chemistry
title: Filtration and Evaporation
welcome_lead: Solids, liquids and a piece of paper: a clever combo to split many mixtures.
meta_desc: Master filtration and evaporation in this KS3 chemistry adventure on separating mixtures.
final_note: You can now separate sand from water and salt from a solution.

concepts.def: Using filter paper to separate insoluble solid from liquid.
The solid left in the filter paper.
The clear liquid that passes through the paper.
Heating a solution so the liquid evaporates, leaving solid behind.
Does not dissolve, e.g. sand in water.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Filtration separates an insoluble solid from a liquid. The mixture is poured through filter paper sat in a funnel.

The solid stays in the paper (residue), and the liquid passes through (filtrate).

To get a soluble solid back out of a solution, gently heat it. The water evaporates away, leaving the solid as crystals.

Salt from salty water.

To purify rock salt (a mixture of salt + sand):

1) Add water — salt dissolves, sand does not.
2) Filter to remove the sand.
3) Evaporate the filtrate to recover the salt.
